notable_absence.finding: As with every other file in this batch, stopping a running rebalance names no specific RBAC role or privilege - only the generic 'unauthorized error' boilerplate. Also absent: any statement of what state the cluster is left in after a stopped rebalance (partially moved data/indexes?) - the DESCRIPTION is a single sentence: 'Stops the currently running rebalance.'

cross_component_finding: rebalance-status.md and rebalance-stop.md are near-identical twins: both have a single-sentence DESCRIPTION, the exact same six-flag OPTIONS block, the same HOST FORMATS/CERTIFICATE AUTHENTICATION/ENVIRONMENT AND CONFIGURATION VARIABLES boilerplate, and a single bare EXAMPLES command differing only in the subcommand name. This IS the sibling-set copy-paste pattern the round's authorship-provenance hypothesis predicts, but it's important to be precise about scope: the duplication is the same universal base-option boilerplate already found on nearly every couchbase-cli subcommand page in this and prior batches (bucket-compact, node-reset, etc.), not something extra or unique to this rebalance/rebalance-status/rebalance-stop trio specifically. Where the trio IS distinctive is terseness: rebalance.md (the full/complex sibling) has a multi-paragraph DESCRIPTION, several unique flags, and five EXAMPLES; its two thinner siblings status/stop each collapse to one sentence of DESCRIPTION and one EXAMPLES command, with literally zero unique flags beyond the shared base six. No CLI-vs-REST/UI terminology drift is verifiable from this page's evidence alone - it introduces no vocabulary of its own to compare.
